title: The Guest Too Large for the Universe
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: The final selection changes scale without changing the moral discipline. The extra-universal guest is formidable enough to endanger three civilisations merely by being present, yet her concrete aim is recognisable—give birth somewhere the child can live—and her willingness to use the cluster if refused remains a real threat. Illuminara's understanding of the distortion as labour must alter the intervention, while staying beside the guest makes love operative and the three powers' independent measurements keep the solution from depending on trust or unlimited magic. The bedside intimacy inside a cosmic emergency offers the day's most surprising emotional register.

Selected candidate C07 (S3). Authorial-core check before prose: protagonist aim = a safe birth for the guest's child and a cluster that remains itself; counterpart (Anomei) wants the child alive and will, if refused, bear it where she stands, which she says plainly; strongest objection on the page (a room offered a closet; the powers' 'a mother's story is what a weapon would tell us'); decisive understanding = the pulse train is labour, its gaps are a convergent series that predicts its own end, and its amplitude measures the room needed, which changes the intervention from containment to relocation; empathy in action = Illuminara stays in the window, carries the threat to the powers unsoftened, and asks rather than commands the Tenders; earned positive outcome = completed birth, restored local physics (clocks agree), bounded Cradle Accord, with the void changed, Chorus songs lost and a unanimity clause that leaves the family's door in four hands. Per the selector's proof test, Illuminara interprets, designs the sealed-prediction and cancel-condition protocol and negotiates; the guest and the powers physically execute (Anomei's own hops, Ussu line-holding song, Halcyon ranging, Kerrel transports).

A strong first draft with a decision-robust plan: the powers never have to trust the guest because the transit is safe even if the worse story is true, sealed predictions and a pre-written cancel condition replace faith, and the pulse clock reconciles to within a few minutes across the day in a spot check. The outcome is real (completed birth, clocks agree, a bounded Accord, costs left visible) and the guest, the three powers and the Tenders keep agency. The weaknesses are all places where the author, reviewing his own work, is most likely to be generous: the one inference that makes the whole rescue possible is narrated rather than shown, two consents come more easily than the text has earned, and the climax and the Accord are told at one remove. Because the author is also the reviewer, these points were chosen by attacking the load-bearing mechanism rather than the prose.

T03 substantially answers the first critique. Corin independently earns the 0.97-light-year room estimate by finding the Wick binary error; Pell receives a real stop condition; the early pulse and shortened final window force different parties to pay visible costs; and the birth produces a child, restored stellar stability and a bounded forty-year hosting agreement without erasing fear or loss. The protagonist's goal, Anomei's goal and the powers' competing belief are all clear, and Illuminara changes the intervention because she first understands each. Three bounded repairs remain: the story must honour the Tender safety threshold when the birth projection crosses it, bind Illuminara's physical intervention to established limits, and make Anomei's assent to the final crossing regime explicit and genuinely reviewable. Preserve the achieved argument, tenderness and positive result while replacing ambiguity rather than adding length.

T05 answered T04 well. The 1.2 light-year rule now governs the birth itself (Pell's two-part condition, the nine-minute evacuation, the cracked glass), the window's act is bounded by consent and by 'what falls inside the window', and the Accord now has a dispute path and Anomei's own statement of what she gives and keeps. The outcome is real and costly: a child is born, the cluster's strain and clocks recover, the Tenders gain a standing hand, and the Rung's glass, two Chorus broods and eight thousand people's day are paid. Because the author is also the reviewer, the three points below were chosen by attacking the load-bearing mechanism rather than the prose. The weakest remaining link is causal: the story asks the reader to believe that the window, not the end of the swell or an error in Corin's model, lowered the core from a projected 1.31 to a measured 0.84, and it asserts that match rather than showing a control. Two lesser issues: length has risen again, and the pulse numbering and the 1.2 / 1.25 / 1.9 figures need one plain reconciliation.
The author delivered the source-bound final after answering the ranked review points and preserving the accepted story line.

An extra-universal mother and four frightened polities freely choose a measurable, consent-bound cradle after Illuminara turns their strongest fear into a test, accepts a bounded physical burden and makes trust unnecessary for the rescue to succeed.
